newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile arrests No.2 colony leader after car chase.
newsitem.headline: Chile arrests No.2 colony leader after car chase.

text.p: Chilean police on Tuesday arrested Hartmut Hopp, a leader of a controversial German colony beset by sex scandal allegations, after a high-speed car chase near the southern town of Linares.

A judge issued an arrest warrant on Monday against Hopp, a doctor at the Colonia Digidad or Dignity Colony, who was accused of covering up child sexual abuse at the settlement and of protecting its fugitive leader Paul Schaefer.
"He was arrested by police early this morning (Tuesday) after a chase which ended when a police vehicle crossed the road and forced him to stop," said Deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco.
Hopp -- widely regarded as Schaefer's No. 2 in the colony -- was detained after a four-mile (6.5 kilometre) chase in rural roads near the town of Linares, 200 miles (320 kms) south of Santiago.
The incident began when Hopp refused to stop at a police road block, said Velasco.
Schaefer, the colony's founder, is the subject of an international arrest warrant after being charged last year with kidnapping and sexually molesting boys at the colony.

Hopp was arrested briefly two weeks ago after he failed to appear before magistrates investigating allegations that he and his wife illegally adopted their teenage son Michael from his biological Chilean mother.
The child's mother Sara Godoy said her son was abducted 10 years ago after she sent him for treatment at the colony's hospital.
Velasco said the judges should also investigate charges made in 1996 that Hopp, now 53, assaulted youngsters at the enclave. Court documents relating to the case have since disappeared.
"If this is investigated and found to be true, then this would change the circumstances. A person accused of the rape of children ... should not be able to adopt a child," he said.
Hopp, who usually acts as the secretive settlement's spokeman, was one of the first youths to come to live at the colony which Schaefer founded in 1961.
Colonia Dignidad's opponents have accused its leaders of holding its some 300 German-speaking residents in virtual slavery, using drugs and electric shock treatment to keep dissidents in line.
The settlers live in Bavarian houses behind barbed-wire at the colony which lies sprawled over valleys and woodland in the foothills of the Andes, near the town of Parral.

Numerous police raids at the colony in recent months have failed to find any trace of Schaefer, although two men who escaped from the colony in July have said he is hiding in a network of tunnels built under forests at the settlement.
One of the men, 24-year old Tobias Muller, has said the colony is protected by the local police.
